tldr: The authors propose GLoRI, a whole-body tracking framework that fuses local motion guidance with world-frame global feedback using cross-attention, demonstrating humanoid loco-manipulation on a real robot that grasps and carries objects at target locations without accumulating drift.
hero_caption: Tracking only local references preserves posture structure but drifts in world-frame position, causing grasp failures. GLoRI shows that explicitly interacting global references and feedback enables closed-loop correction of placement errors without breaking motion coordination.
overview:
When a humanoid robot manipulates objects while walking (loco-manipulation), an error of just a few centimeters at the hands or torso causes grasping to fail. Traditional imitation learning controllers mostly supply target poses in the robot's local frame to leverage translation invariance. However, while this tells the robot 'how to pose,' it provides no explicit constraint on 'where in the world frame to reach.' As tiny foot-slipping errors accumulate during locomotion, the robot fails to reach the target object. On the other hand, while some teleoperation works incorporate global coordinates, how to harmonize global corrections with local coordinated motion patterns during autonomous operation remained unsolved.

To address this, the authors developed GLoRI, a closed-loop tracking controller that harmonizes global and local reference information. Taking only sparse references—three keypoints (head and both hands) plus a root trajectory—GLoRI-Net uses Global-Local Cross Attention (GLCA) to correct global positioning errors without disrupting local motion coordination.

In evaluations, GLoRI achieved a 100% completion rate and slashed tracking error (g-MPJPE) on unseen motions by 45.6% compared to the prior state-of-the-art CLOT (from 11.84 cm down to 6.44 cm). Furthermore, policies trained in Isaac Gym transferred zero-shot to MuJoCo without fine-tuning, demonstrating strong robustness. On a real Unitree G1 robot, using only portable VIVE tracker feedback for root localization, it successfully carried boxes and picked up bags and pillows.
contributions: Proposed GLoRI, a closed-loop tracking framework enabling precise whole-body physical interaction using only sparse keypoint references (head, both hands, and root).

Developed Global-Local Cross Attention (GLCA), which treats local motion priors as queries and injects global targets and pose differences as keys and values to correct global placement without breaking coordinated motion.
Achieved zero-shot sim-to-sim transfer from Isaac Gym to MuJoCo, and demonstrated autonomous loco-manipulation on a real Unitree G1 robot without external motion capture systems.

sections.heading: Why is it so hard for humanoids to walk and grasp at the same time?
sections.summary: In loco-manipulation, positioning errors of just a few centimeters directly cause task failure, making both coordinated motion and absolute world-frame placement indispensable. However, conventional local formulations accumulate global drift, while teleoperation-oriented global methods lack human manual corrections during autonomous execution.
sections.details:
For humanoid robots to assist humans in factories or homes, loco-manipulation—manipulating objects while navigating environments—is essential. Unlike pure locomotion or gesturing, physical interaction is extremely sensitive to spatial accuracy. A slight error in the root (pelvis) or hand placement causes the grasp to miss entirely.

Recent advances in deep reinforcement learning for motion imitation have enabled unified whole-body coordination. However, existing controllers face two main barriers to autonomous loco-manipulation:

- Reliance on local frames: Providing target poses in the robot's local frame offers robustness to environmental shifts, but it leaves 'where in the world frame the motion occurs' unconstrained. Micro-slips during walking accumulate, leaving the hands grasping thin air.
- Lack of autonomous correction mechanisms: Recent teleoperation controllers have started incorporating global positions, but they assume a human operator is monitoring and correcting errors in real time. In autonomous setups where Vision-Language-Action (VLA) models generate targets, human correction is absent, making autonomous global tracking accuracy critical.

GLoRI addresses these challenges by taking sparse reference points (head, both hands, and root trajectory) and explicitly modeling the global-local interaction inside the network, simultaneously realizing natural whole-body coordination and centimeter-to-millimeter placement accuracy.

sections.heading: The evolution of learning-based whole-body control and global feedback
sections.summary: Whole-body control has shifted from model-based methods to reinforcement learning-based motion imitation, and recently toward teleoperation. However, existing global feedback approaches merely concatenate features, failing to properly harmonize motion structure preservation with placement correction.
sections.details:
Humanoid whole-body control has evolved through three main lineages:

### Learning-Based Whole-Body Control
The field shifted from classical Inverse Kinematics (IK) and Model Predictive Control (MPC) to motion imitation via reinforcement learning (RL) in physics simulators. Utilizing large motion capture datasets enabled the reproduction of diverse human movements. However, most of these works supplied reference trajectories in the robot's local frame, without tackling strict positioning in the world frame.

### Whole-Body Control for Loco-Manipulation
Active research has addressed simultaneous walking and upper-body manipulation via teleoperation. Frameworks like TWIST2 used VR devices to control the entire body, but they still centered on relative coordinate frames and lacked the absolute placement constraints needed for precise interaction.

### Emergence of Closed-Loop Global Whole-Body Control
To prevent drift over long-horizon locomotion, approaches like CLONE, CLOT, and ScaleBFM began incorporating global feedback. However, these prior methods often simply concatenate local features and global observations before feeding them to an MLP, lacking a structural understanding of how to maintain local movement patterns while correcting with global errors. GLoRI sets itself apart by explicitly decoupling and harmonizing this interaction via an attention mechanism.

sections.heading: Inside GLoRI: Sharpening local motion with global targets via GLCA
sections.summary: GLoRI decomposes sparse reference inputs—head, both hands, and root—into local motion and global information. At its core, GLoRI-Net uses Global-Local Cross Attention (GLCA), where local tokens query global keys/values, to correct positioning errors in closed loop while preserving coordinated motion.
sections.details:
GLoRI is designed to combine a sparse interface that easily connects with high-level AI models with high-precision closed-loop tracking.

### Task Formulation & Observation Design
The robot is modeled as a 29-DoF Unitree G1. The policy outputs joint residual targets relative to a nominal standing pose, which are executed by PD controllers. Instead of receiving dense whole-body joint angles, the reference targets consist only of the future $H=20$ frames of poses for three keypoints (head, left hand, right hand) and the root trajectory. Observations have clearly separated roles:

- Local Reference: Head and dual-hand poses represented in the reference root frame (18 dimensions). It conveys 'how to move'—the coordinated motion pattern.
- Global Motion Reference: World-frame keypoint targets, relative targets from the current root, and world-frame differences from current keypoints (tracking errors). It conveys 'where to place the hands' and 'how far off they currently are.'
- Global Root Reference: Target root position, orientation, linear/angular velocities in the world frame, and the current root tracking error (72 dimensions). This drives overall translation and heading.

### Network Architecture: GLoRI-Net
Simply concatenating local and global features causes the network to struggle between preserving motion shape and correcting position. To solve this, Global-Local Cross Attention (GLCA) is introduced.

Local motion tokens serve as Queries, while global motion tokens serve as Keys and Values. This direction ensures that the local motion structure acts as the foundation, onto which global placement corrections are added via residual connections. Because the root serves as the origin for the local frame and lacks a local counterpart, it is excluded from GLCA. Instead, it is processed by an independent encoder, concatenated with the attention output, and aggregated across time with 1D temporal convolutions.

### Reward Design and PPO Training
The policy is trained with PPO using joint, keypoint, and root position/velocity tracking rewards, along with regularization terms for smoothness. Although the policy only observes three keypoints, dense whole-body reference data is used for auxiliary rewards during training to guide stable, natural body motions.

captions.F3: Overall architecture of GLoRI-Net. Local motion features serve as Queries and global motion features as Keys/Values in GLCA, after which the refined features are concatenated with root features and aggregated across time.

sections.heading: Experimental results: 100% completion on unseen motions, zero-shot transfer, and real-robot success
sections.summary: On the unseen HuMoTo dataset, GLoRI outperformed prior methods with a 6.44 cm tracking error and a 100% completion rate. It transferred zero-shot from Isaac Gym to MuJoCo and demonstrated high success rates in autonomous loco-manipulation on a real Unitree G1 using a VIVE tracker.
sections.details:
GLoRI's tracking accuracy and generalization were thoroughly validated in simulation and on a physical Unitree G1 robot.

### Simulation Tracking Accuracy and Comparisons
Comparative evaluations on the held-out HuMoTo motion dataset yielded notable results:

- TWIST2, which tracks only local references, achieved good root-aligned error (RA-MPJPE), but its world-frame error (g-MPJPE) diverged significantly, causing frequent task failures.
- Compared to methods tracking dense whole-body global references such as CLOT (g-MPJPE: 11.84 cm) and ScaleBFM (g-MPJPE: 9.38 cm), GLoRI—using only three sparse keypoints—achieved a g-MPJPE of 6.44 cm (a 45.6% error reduction) and a 100% completion rate.
- In ablation experiments, replacing GLCA with direct concatenation (Direct Fusion) degraded g-MPJPE from 4.47 cm to 5.39 cm, confirming the efficacy of the proposed interaction mechanism.

### Sim-to-Sim Transfer (Isaac Gym to MuJoCo)
Without any fine-tuning, the policy trained in Isaac Gym was deployed directly into MuJoCo, which has different contact dynamics. It maintained a 96.97% completion rate on seen motions and 93.9% on unseen motions (g-MPJPE: 7.53 cm), demonstrating strong robustness to physics engine discrepancies.

### Autonomous Manipulation on the Real Unitree G1
In real-robot experiments, instead of a large-scale external motion capture system (such as OptiTrack), a commercially available, portable VIVE Tracker 3.0 was mounted on the waist to provide root pose feedback. Using pre-recorded motion sequences as offline references without real-time human intervention, three tasks were evaluated over three trials each:

- Carry Box: 2 out of 3 successful
- Pick Bag: 2 out of 3 successful
- Pick Pillow: 3 out of 3 successful (100%)

Overall, the robot succeeded in 7 out of 9 trials, proving that complex loco-manipulation can be reliably achieved in the real world using only sparse keypoint references and portable root localization.

sections.heading: Conclusion and future outlook: Integrating with high-level AI models
sections.summary: By resolving the interaction between global targets and local motion, GLoRI achieves high-precision humanoid loco-manipulation. Future work aims to integrate the controller with visuomotor policies and VLA models for fully autonomous task execution.
sections.details:
This work establishes GLoRI as a framework for humanoid robots to operate accurately within a global world while preserving smooth, human-like whole-body coordination. GLCA, the core of GLoRI-Net, proves that global errors can be corrected effectively without distorting local motion structures.

Looking ahead, the authors plan to leverage the sparse interface (head, dual hands, and root) to achieve end-to-end integration with open-vocabulary Vision-Language-Action (VLA) models and egocentric visuomotor policies. GLoRI marks an important milestone as a robust low-level controller that reliably executes high-level AI-generated motion targets in the physical world.

takeaways: Cross-attention (GLCA)—using local references that capture 'how to pose' as Queries and global references that indicate 'where to reach' as Keys/Values—is an effective best practice to eliminate spatial drift without breaking motion coordination.
High-precision whole-body loco-manipulation does not require dense joint trajectories; sparse keypoints (head, dual hands, and root trajectory) are fully sufficient.
Closed-loop real-robot control is practical without expensive optical motion capture rooms, provided portable root pose feedback (such as a VIVE tracker) is available.
limitations: Real-robot experiments tracked pre-recorded offline trajectories; closed-loop adaptation to dynamic environments with real-time targets generated from vision sensors was not demonstrated.
Global root localization still relies on an external VIVE tracker and base stations, falling short of a truly onboard, self-contained system (e.g., pure VIO or SLAM).
Real-robot task evaluation was limited to a pilot scale of 9 trials (7 successes), and recovery behaviors following grasp failures were not incorporated.
